subject: Evidence handling: temporary preservation window and deletion triggers
messages:

Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Incident follow-up: forensic evidence preservation questions

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the quick post-incident sync this morning. We have a couple of immediate questions from our legal and security teams about how you handle evidence after an incident so we can finalize our internal preservation notice. Specific asks:

- How long do you keep per-customer forensic logs and environment snapshots by default after an incident?
- What is the process and lead time to request an extended hold (we may need 12 months)?
- Do preserved artifacts include runtime KV cache snapshots and full request payloads (tokenized user inputs)?
- What guarantees exist around immutability and chain-of-custody for exported artifacts?

Also attaching a sample of the syslog excerpt we captured this morning for context (syslog-sample.tar.gz). Please point us to any forms or agreements we need to sign.

Appreciate a concise list of steps we should follow.

Best,
Jill
Director, Security Operations
Acme Corp

Hi Jill — thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I also attached our internal Forensics Preservation Checklist for reference. If you want a formal legal hold I can open the DocuSign template and route it to your legal contact.

Summary (short):
- Default post-incident preservation window: 90 days for detailed forensic exports (logs, controller traces, routing metadata).
- Extended preservation: can be requested for up to 12 months (or longer with an enterprise agreement) via a preservation request ticket + signed form; typical confirmation within 48 hours.
- Scope: preserved artifacts include system logs, request/response metadata, and optional KV cache snapshots. Full user-input payloads (raw token streams) are NOT included by default unless customer authorization is provided due to privacy concerns; we can include them if Acme signs the preservation scope.
- Immutability/chain-of-custody: exports are stored in an immutable (WORM) S3 bucket with object versioning and an audit trail; we provide export manifests and a signed hash (SHA256) on request.

Practical steps to request extended preservation:
1) Reply to this thread confirming Acme's case ID and requested preservation period.
2) We will open a preservation ticket and send the DocuSign preservation agreement (see link).
3) Once signed, we snapshot the requested artifacts into a WORM bucket with time-stamped manifest and notify your security contact.
4) Exports can be delivered via a secure transfer (S3 presigned URL, SFTP) within 5–10 business days.

A couple things to note: we encrypt artifacts at rest with customer-managed KMS if requested (we support customer CMK integration) and will not include KMS keys in exports. If you need keys for decryption, that requires a separate key escrow/legal process.

I've attached the checklist: redwood_forensics_checklist.xlsx. Let me know if you want me to start the DocuSign workflow.

—Rishi
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi. A few clarifying points from our side:

- Scope: when you say "request/response metadata" can you confirm whether that includes full prompt text and any tool/function call details? Our legal team will likely want the full prompt stream.
- Caches: our engineering team is specifically asking whether the KV cache snapshot contains user identifiers or partial prompt text — if so, we need that included.
- Deletion: once the preservation period ends and you delete artifacts, do you provide a certificate of deletion or signed attestation? Can deletion be performed earlier if we ask?
- Timeline: 48 hours to confirm preservation is great; can you confirm the maximum SLA for exporting artifacts once the agreement is signed? We want to set internal expectations around a 2 week max window.

If it helps, please mark the DocuSign template for 12 months and we'll get it to legal. Also, please call out any regional residency implications — we need all preserved data to remain in US regions.

-Jill
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Incident follow-up: forensic evidence preservation questions

Jill — answers inline below. Long-form so you can share with legal/engineering.

1) Prompt text / tool calls:
- By default we exclude full raw prompt text to minimize exposure; however Acme can opt-in to include prompt streams in preserved exports. When included, prompt text and function/tool-call traces are captured as separate files in the export bundle with clear labeling. Inclusion requires explicit authorization on the preservation agreement to satisfy privacy and data minimization controls.

2) KV cache snapshots & identifiers:
- KV snapshots may contain derived tokens and short-lived keys that reference session IDs. They do not contain plaintext access credentials. If you require PII or identifier redaction, we can run a targeted redaction step prior to export, or include the raw snapshot if you accept that scope in writing.

3) Deletion & attestation:
- Deletion process: after the preservation period we perform a three-step deletion: (a) mark objects for deletion and annul immutability flags, (b) securely purge objects from S3 with overwrite metadata, and (c) rotate and delete export keys.
- Attestation: we provide a signed certificate of deletion (PDF) containing the manifest of deleted objects, deletion timestamps, and the SHA256 of deleted archive manifests. You may also request a notarized attestation under enterprise contract.
- Early deletion: yes — customers can request early deletion via a support ticket; we require the same signed attestation flow to confirm the request.

4) Export SLA:
- Confirm preservation: typically 48 hours.
- Export delivery after signed agreement: goal is within 5 business days; maximum SLA is 10 business days for large datasets. If you need guaranteed 2-week delivery for planning, we will commit to 10 business days max in the preservation agreement.

5) Regional residency:
- We will keep preserved artifacts in US-only regions for Acme when requested; the preservation agreement will include the region (we default to us-east-1).

6) Chain-of-custody / immutability:
- Exports include a manifest and signed SHA256. All preservation actions are logged in Redwood audit logs (timestamped, actor, IP). We store the export in a WORM-enabled bucket with object-lock for the requested period.

Next steps I can take now:
- Open the DocuSign 12-month preservation agreement and route to your legal contact.
- Start the snapshot job once the agreement is signed and provide manifest + presigned S3 URL.

If you want, I'll also loop in our forensics engineer (Mina) to schedule a 30-minute tech call to walk through the export layout and redaction options.

—Rishi
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
